      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Avoid sending prefilled extrapool transactions back to the peers that announced them",
      "quote": "We can reduce a bit of redundancy by not sending them again to the peers that announced them to us.",

      "status": "answered",

      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:4871590805",
      "status_by_quote": "Even if a peer has sent us a transaction that ends up in our extrapool, they may not have it in their mempool now"
    },

      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added redundant prefill logging to the PR",

        "c:4871590805"
      ],

      "status_by_id": "c:4871590805",

      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "style",
      "text": "Prefer WITH_LOCK when reading send_state",

      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author applied the suggestion",

        "rc:3516788147"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],

      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Hoist cb_fut and prefilled_cb_fut out to release m_most_recent_block_mutex before executing syscalls",
      "quote": "I think we can hoist cb_fut and prefilled_cb_fut out and copy the shared futures while m_most_recent_block_mutex is held, then release the lock for the rest of this method.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author released the lock earlier",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3516788330"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3516788330",
      "status_by_quote": "Nice! Much better to not hold a lock that prevents block updates while doing syscalls!!"
    },

      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Avoid switching serialization launch policy from deferred to async",

      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "reviewer edited to note eager background serialization makes sense for prefill, and author asked if resolved",

        "rc:3583336244"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3583336244",

    },

      "status_by_id": "rc:3583342289",
      "status_by_quote": "right now the issue is that we'll update the prefill candidates on reconstruction, but the block might still fail somewhere in ProcessBlock()"

      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Seeding prefill candidates with the coinbase forces unnecessary TCP syscalls and prefill branch execution even when no extra transactions are prefilled",

      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author changed the condition to require more than one candidate",

        "rc:3583340609"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3583340609",

    },
    {

      "kind": "approach",

claims.text: Avoid sending prefilled extrapool transactions back to the peers that announced them
claims.quote: We can reduce a bit of redundancy by not sending them again to the peers that announced them to us.
claims.status_note: author explained that transactions might have been evicted or RBF'd and per-peer tracking adds high complexity
claims.status_by_quote: Even if a peer has sent us a transaction that ends up in our extrapool, they may not have it in their mempool now

claims.text: Logging all required transactions in non-test settings could cause log rate-limiting
claims.quote: Could this cause log rate-limiting? Maybe a good use for the trace log level?
claims.status_note: author replied noting trace and debug logs are not rate limited, and switched to trace logging
claims.status_by_quote: Trace and Debug level logs are not rate limited

claims.text: Log information about wasted prefill bandwidth on the receiving side
claims.quote: An idea mentioned in the delving post was to log information about wasted prefill bandwidth on the receiving side.
claims.status_note: author added redundant prefill logging to the PR
claims.status_by_quote: That's a great point, I had logic for this in my observation nodes, but I've incorporated the changes into this PR.

claims.quote: Since we are just reading the send_state why not prefer WITH_LOCK?

claims.text: Hoist cb_fut and prefilled_cb_fut out to release m_most_recent_block_mutex before executing syscalls
claims.quote: I think we can hoist cb_fut and prefilled_cb_fut out and copy the shared futures while m_most_recent_block_mutex is held, then release the lock for the rest of this method.
claims.status_by_quote: Nice! Much better to not hold a lock that prevents block updates while doing syscalls!!

claims.text: Avoid switching serialization launch policy from deferred to async
claims.quote: I don't think we should be switching the serialization from std::launch::deferred to std::launch::async.
claims.status_note: reviewer edited to note eager background serialization makes sense for prefill, and author asked if resolved
claims.status_by_quote: Yeah, sorry if it's weird to combine both changes in one commit, I can split up if you think that makes sense.

claims.text: When will the block hash in prefill_candidates differ from hash, and can they be merged?
claims.quote: When will the block hash in prefill_candidates differ from hash above? Can these be merged?
claims.status_note: author explained candidates update on reconstruction but the block might still fail in ProcessBlock
claims.status_by_quote: right now the issue is that we'll update the prefill candidates on reconstruction, but the block might still fail somewhere in ProcessBlock()

claims.text: Remove duplicate logging of window_size and bytes_available
claims.quote: We log window_size and bytes_available here, but we also log them on the call side. Can we remove one of the logs?
claims.status_by_quote: Ok, I removed it on the caller side.

claims.text: Seeding prefill candidates with the coinbase forces unnecessary TCP syscalls and prefill branch execution even when no extra transactions are prefilled
claims.quote: In that case, the check in net_processing for prefill_candidates.size() > 0 is always true, so we will always go through the prefill path and do all the syscalls even for the current behavior of alway
claims.status_note: author changed the condition to require more than one candidate
claims.status_by_quote: Great catch, thank you, I took this by changing the check to be prefill_candidates.size() > 1

claims.text: Avoid taking and releasing m_send_mutex multiple times by returning early
claims.quote: we should take m_send_mutex lock and return the value if send_state != SendState::v1, and then return the fallback after releasing the lock.
claims.status_note: author refactored lock handling and header size method
claims.status_by_quote: Taken thanks, this also made me realize GetMessageHeaderSize shouldn't be virtual, public, or take a lock, so fixed that as well.

claims.text: Use-after-free by resetting txn_available before retrieving its size
claims.quote: This is a use-after-free. We need to get the size before we reset it 3 lines above.
claims.status_by_quote: Thanks for catching, sorry the quality of this logging commit was low when I pushed it.

claims.text: Logging fails to increment prefilled_size and fails to adjust extra_size
claims.quote: Also need prefilled_size += tx_size; We don't increment/decrement extra_size either. Seems like an oversight?
claims.status_note: author acknowledged and resolved logging omissions
claims.status_by_quote: Thanks for catching, sorry this went out broken.

claims.text: Why redundant mempool stats are handled under a not-in-mempool condition
claims.quote: why inside this condition !pool->exists(tx_wtxid) which means "not in mempool", there's a mempool variable redundant_prefilled_mp_... handling?
claims.status_note: fixed when logging was extracted into PR 35724 and rebased
claims.status_by_quote: I'll let both my comments open, although I see they are fixed in #35724.

claims.text: prefilled_size is never incremented, resulting in inaccurate reconstruction log stats
claims.quote: the value is always zero. Which could not be true in any scenario as coinbase is always prefilled. I couldn't find any assignment to it, probably it's a simple fix.
claims.status_note: author resolved by rebasing on top of logging PR 35724
claims.status_by_quote: Thanks, I've rebased this on #35724, so marking as resolved.
